correctness.rationale: In affine barycentric coordinates, skeleton membership is support size <=r+1. The sparse-splitting lemma for masses w_i>=0 summing to k with at most kr+1 positions is proved inductively. In sorted order choose the first consecutive length-r block of mass <=1. A predecessor entry (or position r+1 if the first block works) has enough mass to complete a probability row of support <=r+1; delete the r exhausted coordinates and repeat. This gives sufficiency. If kr<d, barycentric target (1-eps,eps/d,...,eps/d), 0<eps<1/k, requires every row to use the dominant vertex, leaving at most kr other positive coordinates; all d are positive, a contradiction. Independently tested 2800 exact rational decompositions across r=1..4 and k=1..7, support/sum/reconstruction, without treating them as all-dimensional proof.
residual_risks: The construction is only for closed simplex skeleta, exact equal-weight summands and all-positive near-vertex witnesses; arbitrary polytopal complexes are not addressed.

value.rationale: Exact finite convexification is a natural invariant of the nonconvex r-skeleton, and the sharp threshold ceils dimension by skeleton dimension for every simplex and all real barycentric weights. It gives a constructive finite cutoff and near-vertex obstruction, not a parameter substitution or an asymptotic rate.

final_claim: For every nondegenerate d-simplex and 1<=r<d, the k-fold equal-weight Minkowski average of the closed r-skeleton equals the entire simplex exactly when kr>=d.
